words.definition: of or relating to knowledge or knowing
words.example: He's a brilliant teacher who has the epistemic humility to know that there is always more to learn.

words.definition: words used only by a particular group
words.example: The novels were such a success that fans began communicating in the secret argot spoken by the series’ characters.

words.definition: exchangeable for something of the same kind or value
words.example: A dollar bill is considered fungible because it can easily and acceptably be traded for ten dimes, four quarters, twenty nickels, or one hundred pennies, as well as any other dollar bill.

words.definition: relating to the sense of touch
words.example: With the introduction of haptics to smartphones, receiving a call from a friend became a much more tactile experience.

words.definition: an expert who offers opinions on a topic
words.example: Grandpa likes watching political pundits spar about the issues of the day on the Sunday morning talk shows.

words.definition: comprehensive; including many, most, or all things
words.example: The coveted book prize was awarded to a compendious history of environmental literature in the United States.

words.definition: an opponent or enemy that is very difficult to defeat
words.example: She will be playing against her old nemesis for the championship.

words.definition: of, relating to, or suggesting a poem or song expressing sorrow
words.example: The elegiac tone of the singer’s first album always leaves me in tears.
